title: What is the sum of the first ten odd numbers?
description: Ten L shaped layers make a ten by ten square grid, so the first ten odd numbers add up to one hundred. Keeko's doubt, that the sum is the number doubled, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of odd numbers added is the side of the square, so the sum is that side times itself. Watch for students who double the number instead of multiplying it by itself.

source: By drawing a similar picture, can you say what is the sum of
video_script.why: The child uses the square grid picture to find the sum of the first ten odd numbers as ten times ten.
video_script.substitution: The sum of the first n odd numbers is the dots of an n by n square.
video_script.anchor: a square grid of dots cut into ten L shaped layers, with the first four layers drawn and the rest dotted
video_script.wrong_answer: the sum is the number doubled
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the sum is the number doubled, so ten odd numbers make twenty. Ten layers make a grid of ten rows and ten columns, so the dots are ten times ten, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum of the first ten odd numbers is one hundred
hold_back: The sum of the first 10 odd numbers is 100
never_show: the sum is the number doubled
maths_rules: each odd number is one L shaped layer, so 10 numbers make 10 layers
10 layers make a 10 by 10 square grid
check: the pairs 1 + 19, 3 + 17, 5 + 15, 7 + 13, 9 + 11 each make 20, and 5 x 20 = 100
slip: doubling 10 gives 20, which is not the sum
video_script.design: One idea: n odd numbers fill an n by n square. Assumes the picture of nested L shapes. Wrong idea: the sum is the number doubled. The grid stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the ten by ten grid with its ten rows and ten columns marked; the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sum is the number doubled, so ten odd numbers make twenty.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>But ten layers make a grid of ten rows and ten columns. That has far more than twenty dots.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The number of layers is multiplied by itself, and it is not doubled.
